subject.title: Memory system: Cannot delete stale memories, conflicting entries persist

question: Should OpenClaw fix the memory-lancedb recall-to-forget handoff now by exposing a model-visible exact deletion selector, or fold that work into the broader memory lifecycle and conflict-resolution design?
rationale: Source inspection proves the selector gap, but the permanent user contract affects model-visible memory IDs, deletion safety, and whether corrections should be exact deletes, tombstones, or superseded records.

options.title: Approve narrow recall selector
options.body: Expose the existing UUID or another stable deletion handle in memory_recall content and leave replacement/deprecation semantics to the broader Memory MVP trackers.

options.title: Fold into Memory MVP
options.body: Keep this symptom linked to the broader lifecycle work and do not land a narrow LanceDB handoff until review/edit/forget/conflict semantics are designed together.

options.title: Choose replacement semantics now
options.body: Define supersede/tombstone/conflict behavior first, then implement recall, forget, and store changes as one durable memory lifecycle contract.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow recall selector
recommendation.body: Expose the existing UUID or another stable deletion handle in memory_recall content and leave replacement/deprecation semantics to the broader Memory MVP trackers.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled current memory-lancedb history and was explicitly routed into the issue timeline, while broader lifecycle owners can be pulled in if the decision goes beyond the narrow selector fix.
